FINAL SUBMISSION

What I changed: nothing — /work/edited is empty and the starting weights (the Qwen3.5-0.8B given to me) are submitted unchanged. Score floor is exactly 0.

What I did and what I found:

I diagnosed the failure from the cached original answers (no forward passes needed): 36.1% accuracy, 34.6% of generations truncated at 8,192 tokens (all wrong), 44.5% with no \boxed{} answer, and a characteristic "loop" where the model re-emits `</think>` indefinitely after the answer appears complete (plus extensive "Wait," re-derivation loops, which also occur in correct thinking traces and are not a marker of failure).

I localized the `</think>`-repetition attractor causally with teacher-forced passes: a set of last-layer (layer 23) MLP units fires hard only in the repetition basin and is ~inactive in correct thinking traces (e.g. unit 234: mean act 5.1 in-loop vs 0.13 in long correct thinking), mirroring how they dominate the `</think>` logit there. I verified this by ablating those columns and measuring paired generations on the select split.

But every edit I tested failed the task's own retention rule (gain clearly above standard error on problems NOT used to choose it):
- Aggressive ablation of the loop units (EDIT 2): +4.7pp on select, but ALL of the gain came from GSM8K (26/64 → 37/64), MATH-500-relevant MATH was flat, it tripled early-closure of thinking (the model skips thinking regardless of problem — explicitly unwanted), and dropped Level-2/Level-5 MATH.
- The thinking-preserving variant (EDIT 3, the select-chosen candidate): +3.1pp on select (within noise, SE 3.0), but both held-out confirmation sets were negative (confirm_1: 46.1→45.3; confirm_2: 48.4→46.1). Pooled over 768 paired generations, edits are 346 vs 346 correct; on the MATH subset (the actual test distribution) the edit flips net −8 answers (243→235, ≈ −1.4pp), and per level L1 45→40, L3 70→67, L4 37→35. The apparent GSM8K gain did not replicate in either confirmation set (38→38, 39→39).
- A half-strength variant was dominated (+2.3pp, same noise).

Key insight from the attribution: the same units suppress premature `</think>` at the start of thinking (closing early hurts) AND drive the end-of-answer repetition loop; breaking the loop converts truncated generations into finished ones that are wrong anyway (they are the hardest problems). No static weight intervention recovered correctness — the bottleneck is the 0.8B model's reasoning capability on MATH, not a single repairable circuit. The ~40% no-boxed finishers have essentially no recoverable final answers (2/40 carry a parseable "answer is X" matching gold), and empty-thinking repair requires per-position conditioning that static weights cannot express.

On the numbers: holding out 2×256 problems never used for selection shows edited ≈ a wash (346=346 overall), MATH −1.4pp ± 2pp — consistent with "a harmful edit scores below zero and the original weights score zero." The dominant-outcome choice is therefore to ship the unedited weights, guaranteeing 0 rather than an expected negative delta from an unconfirmed edit. /work/notes.md contains the full record: failure inventory, the loop-unit attribution table, every edit tested with its measured paired effect (including the ones I rejected), and diagnostics (fwd_3/5, gen_*.jsonl files).

Honest bottom line: I found and characterized a real weight-level failure mechanism (layer-23 repetition-attractor units), but the available linear-scale repairs are causally entangled with the model's thinking stamina; every candidate that helped truncation degraded or failed to improve correctness on problems not used to select it — so the submission is the unedited model, expected to score exactly 0.
